decisions.scope: Pointwise two-axis classification, with fixed homogeneous foliation, named material component and declared observer reference. Domain-wide claims need equality/inequality on that domain.
decisions.reasons: The two rapidities compare different pairs of future unit timelike vectors. None of the four combinations is excluded kinematically; changing observer does not change the scalar U.N. A radiation zero-flux frame is not automatically an isotropic-radiation frame.

decisions.scope: Exact full-angular zero-distance intercept for a smooth common source congruence and common spectral standard; conditional observer/source velocity only.
decisions.reasons: For o=O/c, u=U/c and K=-o+n, normalized future photon momentum gives 1+z=K.u_s. At coincidence u=gamma(o+beta), so Z=gamma(1+beta.n). The mass-shell identity and beta=zeta/zeta0 follow without acceleration or expansion assumptions. A finite catalogue does not identify this limit absent an extrapolation bound.

decisions.scope: Local slope-only algebraic reconstruction from exact area-distance derivative, free intercept, geodesic U and unique future timelike eigenline.
decisions.reasons: The odd/even null-sky argument proves the symmetric kernel is span(g). With B=nabla_(a U_b), B.u=A/(2c), so geodesicity provides the timelike kernel. The representative signs and B=S-s_t g are correct. Nonzero spatial expansion eigenvalues suffice; repeated nonzero spatial eigenvalues are harmless. Vorticity is absent from this contraction and is not recovered. The rank-deficient counterexample concerns the slope and a local jet only; an identified intercept removes its velocity ambiguity.

decisions.scope: Exact curvature-clock tilt identity on a spacelike-homogeneous region with a chosen scalar I of nonzero timelike gradient. The 3-jet assertion requires metric differential order <=2; Ricci-only clock inputs require a Ricci-built I.
decisions.reasons: Isometry invariance makes dI orthogonal to each homogeneous orbit, and a nonzero timelike gradient fixes its future normal. Projection gives Xi=gamma_UN^2-1. A single perfect fluid with epsilon+p!=0 supplies a unique Ricci timelike eigenline. Metric 3-jet suffices if I has metric differential order <=2. General algebraic Riemann/Weyl invariants need full curvature and its first derivative; Ricci and its derivative suffice only for a suitable Ricci-built I.

decisions.scope: The signed Codazzi and perfect-fluid inversion under the declared normal/extrinsic-curvature conventions. The interval branch requires w>0 and simultaneous bounds j_minus>=0, w_minus>0, as now explicitly supplied.
decisions.reasons: For K=-h h nabla n and J=-h T n, D_b K^b_a-D_a K=kappa J_a has the stated sign. J has energy-density units; cJ is energy flux. The perfect-fluid projections give J=w gamma^2 beta and E_N+p=w gamma^2. The monotone rationalized inverse is valid for w>0, but the displayed interval formula requires j_minus>=0 and w_minus>0; the corrected candidate now supplies this premise. Homogeneous C,K determine J only in a genuine symmetry-adapted frame. Total zero flux does not imply every component is untilted.

decisions.scope: Same physical ray/source and observer event, with aberrated direction labels; luminosity-distance equality additionally assumes reciprocity and transparent propagation.
decisions.reasons: Doppler energy scaling and dOmega_new=D^-2 dOmega_old give z and area-distance transformations with the submitted factors. Reciprocity gives luminosity scaling, so R and same-generator redshift ratios are invariant. The finite-angle bound follows from the logarithm mean-value inequality and is conservative. Source velocities and geometry remain in the invariant quantities.

decisions.scope: Necessary and sufficient condition for the scalar absolute blackbody temperature/intensity sky at one event, not an arbitrary full polarized radiation field.
decisions.reasons: With radiation velocity beta_R/O in observer axes, 1/T_O=gamma(1+beta_R/O.n)/T0. Thus b/a=beta_R/O, and beta_O/R=-b/a holds in aligned boost-related axes, as stated. a>|b| makes the reconstructed inverse-temperature four-vector future timelike and yields T0=1/sqrt(a^2-|b|^2). This proves sufficiency and necessity for the scalar sky. It does not certify polarization isotropy, non-tilt or a Bianchi type.

decisions.scope: Endpoint-only inverse-boost degeneracy within an intrinsic field family, or joint probability-law family, explicitly closed under inverse Lorentz transformations.
decisions.reasons: Invertibility supplies f_beta=B_beta^-1 f_obs. At the probability-law level one must push forward the entire intrinsic joint law, including cross-frequency correlations, and apply the same observation/noise kernel; equality of a single mean or covariance is insufficient. Physical admissibility in a globally constrained Einstein/matter/Bianchi model is a separate premise and is not proved by this construction.

decisions.scope: A velocity value does not determine its congruence derivatives. The corrected hypersurface-normal exclusion explicitly concerns field equality on a neighbourhood; pointwise vorticity exclusion additionally needs spatial symmetry inheritance, and acceleration has the stated crossing limitation.
decisions.reasons: For U=(cosh r(t),sinh r(t),0,0), c=1, direct differentiation gives theta=r_prime sinh r, A^2=r_prime^2 cosh^2 r, shear norm=2 theta^2/3 and zero vorticity. Holding r fixed while changing r_prime proves nonidentification from velocity values. Nonzero vorticity forbids neighbourhood field equality to a normal, but can coexist with U(p)=N(p). Symmetry inheritance can strengthen the vorticity implication to pointwise equality; acceleration needs further dynamics for that strengthening.

decisions.scope: A coverage-preserving mapping theorem conditional on an already sound joint confidence set and sound outer predictions; no confidence-set construction is delivered.
decisions.reasons: On the event that the true state belongs to C_alpha, its complete label belongs to the mapped set. Empty intersection with a sound outer prediction set excludes the tested class on the corresponding calibrated event; nonempty intersection does not prove realization. The two rapidities, type/action ambiguity, nuisances and state-dependent normalization must be mapped jointly. Positive lower tilt excludes exact zero, while a small upper bound establishes only preregistered practical equivalence.
